1 · The ★ Principle
FOUNDING PRINCIPLE

Measure what is left over after an interaction. Admit only what fits inside that leftover.
Otherwise refuse — and record the refusal.

Every interaction produces a surplus. Two things meet, something happens, and what remains
afterward is what's real. Everything else — expectations, projections, hopes — is claim.
★ reverses the default order. Most systems admit inputs then check them: open the door, then look at
who walked in. ★ measures the capacity first and admits only what fits.

★ in the Ledger
refuse()

doesn't just reject — it records what was refused and why, creating a permanent trail of

every boundary decision. A refusal is itself a measurement.

★ in the Vault
Measures shard health, computes whether recovery fits inside the redundancy leftover, refuses

★ is not a filter. It is a measurement instrument.

2 · The Three Laws of Data
LAW 1

Never estimate. No "~", no rounding. Measured or uncounted.

A "~500" is not data — it's a story about data. The pipeline flags estimates as UNRESOLVED, never
MEASURED.

LAW 2

Language never distorts data. Figures carry exact values with plain labels. Interpretation is
quarantined.

"Thermal = 5.59" is data. "Thermal is elevated" is interpretation. Different fields, never mixed.

LAW 3

Zero is ignition. Origin, start of a new cycle — never mere absence.

The Ledger's genesis hash is "GENESIS" — a presence, not an absence. Every entry hashes back to
it.

3 disagreements → stop. Rethink. Never grind.

An agent author and reviewer once went 50+ rounds overnight. The code didn't improve after round 3

Diminishing returns are a signal, not a failure.

4 · Clean-Room Verification
1. Investigator writes SPEC (no original material).
2. Builder sees only the spec. Builds blind.
3. Comparator runs 50 inputs: 30 normal, 10 edge, 10 error.
All 50 must match. If the builder needs the original, the room is broken — rewrite the spec.

A chimera fuses the strongest traits of different beasts into one organism. CHIMERA fuses five
verification traditions into a single Python file with zero dependencies.

DEFINITION

CHIMERA is a deterministic verification pipeline that treats every claim as guilty until
proven innocent — innocent meaning "survived every boring explanation."

It doesn't generate ideas. It doesn't write prose. It takes a claim, attacks it eight ways, and reports
what survived. The output isn't a verdict — it's a corpse count.

CHIMERA Vol. IV — Proof

1 · Why Arguments Fail
An argument can be refused. A sufficiently motivated AI — or human — can argue with any prose,
any chart, any expert consensus. Arguments depend on the listener's willingness to be convinced.
A sealed computation cannot be argued with. It can only be reproduced or broken. There is no third
option. The listener's willingness is irrelevant — the SHA-256 either matches or it doesn't.

Agreement is not requested. It is computed.

2 · What a Proof Is
DEFINITION

A proof is a sealed computation: deterministic code + fixed inputs + hashed outputs,
verifiable to byte-identical results by any party.

A proof.json contains:

3 · The Sealing Process
python3 proof.py seal

performs five steps:

① Hash the code. SHA-256 of chimera_pipeline.py and proof.py . If either changes by one
byte, verification halts.

② Run deterministically. Fixed seed (48), fixed permutation count (1500), fixed data (recomputed
from formula). No randomness, no network, no time-dependence.

③ Hash inputs and outputs. Canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace variation) → SHA-256.
The output hash is the proof's fingerprint.

④ Record in ledger. The sealing event goes into the hash-chained ledger: proof name, all hashes,
elapsed time.

⑤ Emit proof.json. The sealed artifact. Portable, self-describing, independently verifiable.

python3 proof.py verify

① Check code integrity. Hash the local pipeline and proof files. Compare to sealed hashes. If
different → HALT: "This is not the proof that was sealed."

② Reproduce. Run the computation with the sealed seed and parameters.
③ Compare hashes. If output hash matches → ✓ VERIFIED. If not → ✗ MISMATCH.
There are exactly two outcomes: verified or broken. No third option exists. That is what makes it
unrefusable.

5 · The Tamper Test
Live test performed 2026-10-17:
Appended # tamper (9 bytes) to chimera_pipeline.py . Ran verification.
Result: HALT — "Code differs from sealed version. This is not the proof that was sealed." The
system refused to even attempt reproduction. Restored the file → verification passed byte-identical.
The tamper test proves the seal isn't decorative. It's structural: the code hash is checked before
reproduction, so a modified pipeline can never produce a "verified" result.

CHIMERA Vol. V — Unchained

1 · The Problem with Parity
XOR parity (RAID-5 era) survives exactly one shard loss. Lose two, and the data is gone. It's 1980s
technology wearing modern clothes.
Reed-Solomon RS(4,2) survives any two of six shard losses. Not "the first two" or "two specific
ones" — any two. That's 21 combinations, all recoverable.

Parity asks "which shard died?" Reed-Solomon asks "how many?"

2 · Reed-Solomon: How It Works
Data is split into k=4 shards. Then m=2 parity shards are computed using Galois Field GF(256)
arithmetic — polynomial evaluation at 6 points, any 4 of which can reconstruct the original.

Encoding

file:///tmp/chimera_light/CHIMERA_Vol5_Unchained_iphone.html

2/5

 10/18/26, 2:43 AM

CHIMERA Vol. V — Unchained

A Vandermonde matrix transforms 4 data shards into 6 coded shards. Each coded shard is a linear
combination (in GF(256)) of the data shards. The math guarantees: pick any 4, solve the linear
system, recover all data.

Decoding
Take any 4 surviving shards. Extract the corresponding 4×4 submatrix. Invert it via Gauss-Jordan
elimination in GF(256). Multiply by the surviving shards. The original data falls out.
If fewer than 4 survive → return None . Not a guess. Not partial data. None — honest refusal.
Pure Python, zero dependencies. GF(256) log/exp tables built at init. ~200 lines.

3 · Merkle Verification
Each shard gets a SHA-256 hash stored in the manifest. On audit, every shard is re-hashed and
compared. Corruption is pinpointed to the exact shard index — no need to read or decode anything
first.
Corrupt shards are treated as missing (set to None ), then Reed-Solomon reconstructs them. After
reconstruction, the reassembled data is hashed against the manifest. If it doesn't match →
"REBUILT BUT HASH MISMATCH — do not trust."

4 · The Vault
The Vault class combines everything:
store(data, name)
audit(name)

— Encode → write 6 shards → write manifest (hashes, lengths, params).

— Check every shard against manifest. Returns list of bad indices and whether

recovery is possible.
recover(name)

— If recoverable: decode, verify hash, rewrite clean shards. If not: honest refusal

with exact counts.

CHIMERA Vol. VI — Axiom

1 · The Problem AXIOM Solves
Anyone can claim anything. A statistic in an article. A result in a paper. A "fact" in a post. There is no
standard way to attach the computation that produced it. Claims float free of their evidence.
AI made this infinitely worse. A language model can produce fluent, confident, fully Hallucinated
statistics — formatted identically to real ones. The reader cannot distinguish them. The format carries
no provenance.

The world's problem isn't lack of information. It's lack of trustable information.

2 · What AXIOM Is
DEFINITION

AXIOM is a protocol — not a platform — for sealing quantitative claims into
independently verifiable proofs. No server. No account. No permission. Just math.

file:///tmp/chimera_light/CHIMERA_Vol6_Axiom_iphone.html

CHIMERA Vol. VI — Axiom

A claim file is any Python script defining compute(seed) → dict . AXIOM seals it into a .ax
proof file containing: the statement, code hash, input hash, output hash, seed, result, parent proofs,
author, and timestamp.
Anyone with the .ax file and the original script runs axiom.py verify and gets byte-identical
results — or exposes the break.

3 · Sealing a Claim
python3 axiom.py seal my_claim.py \
--statement "Mean response time is 42ms" \
--author "taylor@monstersink" --seed 48

What happens:
1. Hash the claim source (SHA-256).
2. Run compute(seed=48) deterministically.
3. Hash inputs and outputs (canonical JSON).
4. Collect parent proof IDs (if this builds on others).
5. Emit my_claim.ax — the sealed proof.
The .ax file is portable, self-describing, and permanent. It doesn't depend on any server staying up.

4 · Verifying a Claim
python3 axiom.py verify my_claim.ax

What happens:
1. Check code integrity — hash local source vs. sealed hash. Modified → HALT.
file:///tmp/chimera_light/CHIMERA_Vol6_Axiom_iphone.html

CHIMERA Vol. VI — Axiom

2. Reproduce — run compute() with the sealed seed.
3. Compare output hashes. Match → ✓ VERIFIED. Mismatch → ✗ BROKEN.
Dispute requires a new proof, not a louder voice.

5 · Proof Chaining
A claim can declare PARENT_PROOFS — IDs of proofs it builds on. This creates a directed acyclic
graph of verified knowledge: each proof's validity depends on its parents' validity, and the whole
chain is auditable.
axiom.py chain

displays the ancestry: every parent, grandparent, and the hashes linking them.

If a parent proof is later broken (non-reproducible), every child is flagged. Truth propagates forward;
breakage propagates backward. The graph is self-healing: replace the broken parent with a valid
proof, and the children re-verify.

6 · The World It Creates
Imagine: every number in every article ships with its .ax file. Every AI claim comes with its proof.
Every statistic links to the computation that produced it.

"""Optimal format + combinations for the pipeline.

1. OPTIMAL FORMAT: a new 'optimal' plugin — compact self-describing binary
   frame for the aggregate report. Measured against JSON on bytes.
2. COMBINATIONS: every scenario x every format, measured. The table picks
   the winner; nothing is guessed.
"""
import io, struct, time
import pipeline_starting_line as P

# --- 1. optimal binary frame -------------------------------------------
# magic "PIPE1" | n_users u8 | per user: name_len u8, name, tier u8,
# total f64, n_cats u8 | per cat: name_len u8, name, amount f64
TIER_CODE = {"StandardTier": 0, "VIPTier": 1}

def encode_optimal(report):
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    users = report["users"]
    buf.write(b"PIPE1")
    buf.write(struct.pack("<B", len(users)))
    for uname, prof in users.items():
        nb = uname.encode()
        buf.write(struct.pack("<B", len(nb)) + nb)
        buf.write(struct.pack("<B", TIER_CODE[prof["tier"]]))
        buf.write(struct.pack("<d", prof["total_spent"]))
        cats = prof["categories"]
        buf.write(struct.pack("<B", len(cats)))
        for cname, amt in cats.items():
            cb = cname.encode()
            buf.write(struct.pack("<B", len(cb)) + cb)
            buf.write(struct.pack("<d", amt))
    return buf.getvalue()

class OptimalSink(P.SinkPlugin, format_name="optimal"):
    def export(self, data):
        return encode_optimal(data)

# --- 2. scenarios --------------------------------------------------------

    {"type": "buy", "user": "  Alice ", "item": {"cat": "Electronics", "price": 300}},

def bulk(n):

SCENARIOS = {

        {"type": "refund", "user": "z"}],
    "bulk_10k": bulk(10_000),
}
FORMATS = ["json", "summary", "optimal"]

def run_once(raw, fmt):
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    bp = (raw | P.parse_events() | P.meter(label="c") |

    for sname, raw in SCENARIOS.items():

"""DERIVE the creative solution: an adaptive exporter.

Evidence (from the combination matrix):
  - optimal binary beats JSON 65-80% on every lossless scenario
  - but the margin varies per user block (small users: JSON overhead dominates
    differently than big users)
Derivation: don't pick ONE format. Measure both per user-segment and admit
the smaller. Record the derivation. This is ★ applied to serialization:
measure the leftover, admit what fits.
"""
import json as _json, struct, io
import pipeline_starting_line as P
from combine_optimal import encode_optimal

DERIVATIONS = []  # the recorded derivation: why each choice was made

def _frag_json(uname, prof):
    return _json.dumps({"users": {uname: prof}}).encode()

def _frag_optimal(uname, prof):
    return encode_optimal({"users": {uname: prof}})

class DeriveSink(P.SinkPlugin, format_name="derive"):
    """Per-segment adaptive format. Frame: PIPE2 | n u8 | per user:
    fmt u8 (0=json,1=optimal) | len u32 | payload. DERIVATIONS logs the why."""
    def export(self, data):
        DERIVATIONS.clear()
        buf = io.BytesIO()
        users = data["users"]
        buf.write(b"PIPE2")
        buf.write(struct.pack("<B", len(users)))
        for uname, prof in users.items():
            fj, fo = _frag_json(uname, prof), _frag_optimal(uname, prof)
            if len(fo) <= len(fj):
                fmt, payload, saved = 1, fo, len(fj) - len(fo)
            else:
                fmt, payload, saved = 0, fj, len(fo) - len(fj)
            DERIVATIONS.append({"user": uname, "chose": "optimal" if fmt else "json",
                                "json_bytes": len(fj), "optimal_bytes": len(fo),
                                "saved": saved})
            buf.write(struct.pack("<B", fmt))
            buf.write(struct.pack("<I", len(payload)))
            buf.write(payload)
        return buf.getvalue()

def decode_derive(blob):
    assert blob[:5] == b"PIPE2", "bad magic"
    n = blob[5]
    pos, out = 6, {"users": {}}
    for _ in range(n):
        fmt = blob[pos]; ln = struct.unpack("<I", blob[pos+1:pos+5])[0]
        payload = blob[pos+5:pos+5+ln]; pos += 5 + ln
        if fmt == 1:
            # optimal fragment: PIPE1 | n=1 | user block — parse minimally
            assert payload[:5] == b"PIPE1"
            p = 6
            nl = payload[p]; uname = payload[p+1:p+1+nl].decode(); p += 1 + nl
            tier = "VIPTier" if payload[p] == 1 else "StandardTier"; p += 1
            total = struct.unpack("<d", payload[p:p+8])[0]; p += 8
            nc = payload[p]; p += 1
            cats = {}
            for _ in range(nc):
                cl = payload[p]; cname = payload[p+1:p+1+cl].decode(); p += 1 + cl
                amt = struct.unpack("<d", payload[p:p+8])[0]; p += 8
                cats[cname] = amt
            out["users"][uname] = {"tier": tier, "total_spent": total,
                                   "categories": cats}
        else:
            out["users"].update(_json.loads(payload)["users"])
    return out

if __name__ == "__main__":
    from combine_optimal import SCENARIOS
    print(f"{'scenario':<14} {'json':>7} {'optimal':>7} {'derive':>7}  verdict")
    for sname, raw in SCENARIOS.items():
        res = {}
        for fmt in ("json", "optimal", "derive"):
            bp = (list(raw) | P.parse_events() | P.run_state_and_aggregate()
                  | P.export_as(fmt=fmt))
            out = bp.unwrap()
            res[fmt] = len(out)
        # round-trip check on derive
        bp = (list(raw) | P.parse_events() | P.run_state_and_aggregate()
              | P.export_as(fmt="derive"))
        rt = decode_derive(bp.unwrap())
        bp2 = (list(raw) | P.parse_events() | P.run_state_and_aggregate()
               | P.export_as(fmt="json"))
        import json as j
        ok = rt == j.loads(bp2.unwrap())
        best = min(res, key=res.get)
        print(f"{sname:<14} {res['json']:>7} {res['optimal']:>7} "
              f"{res['derive']:>7}  {best} wins, round-trip {'OK' if ok else 'FAIL'}")
    print("\nDerivation log (last scenario):")
    for d in DERIVATIONS[:8]:
        print(f"  {d['user']}: chose {d['chose']} "
              f"(json {d['json_bytes']}B vs optimal {d['optimal_bytes']}B, "
              f"saved {d['saved']}B)")
    if len(DERIVATIONS) > 8:
        print(f"  ... +{len(DERIVATIONS)-8} more")

"""PIPELINE — value-of-information edition, 2026-10-17.

Converted from the monetary pipeline (pipeline_final.py). The machinery is
identical — only the tracked quantity changes:

  dollars  ->  bits of verified information
  purchase ->  signal (an interaction yielding measured information)
  refund   ->  retraction (information refuted or withdrawn; resets accumulation)
  category ->  channel (where the signal came from)
  VIP $500 ->  VIP at 500 verified bits

Semantics (the ★ principle): every signal is an interaction. The pipeline
measures what is left over (verified bits), admits what fits (accumulates),
and refuses the rest — recording each refusal in quarantine. A retraction
zeroes the ledger: refuted information un-accumulates.

Units are honest: 'bits' here means measured verification units admitted by
the pipeline's own validators. The pipeline does not estimate information
content; it records what its instruments measured.

Run:  python3 pipeline_voi.py
"""
from pipeline_final import (
    Pipe, BoundPipe, Validated, clean_str, positive_num,
    SinkPlugin, JSONSink, SummarySink, OptimalSink,
    QuarantineSink, AlertSink, Tree,
    parse_events as _parse_events_base,
    meter, tee, export_as, METERS, QUARANTINE,
)
from collections import defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass
import json as _json


# ===========================================================================
# DOMAIN — signals and retractions
# ===========================================================================
class SignalEvent:
    """One interaction that yielded measured information."""
    user = Validated(clean_str)
    channel = Validated(clean_str)
    bits = Validated(positive_num)

    def __init__(self, user, channel, bits):
        self.user = user
        self.channel = channel
        self.bits = bits


@dataclass
class RetractionEvent:
    """Information withdrawn or refuted — accumulation resets."""
    user: str


@dataclass
class StandardTier:
    bits: float = 0.0


@dataclass
class VIPTier:
    bits: float
    perks_unlocked: bool = True


VOI_VIP_THRESHOLD = 500.0  # verified bits to reach VIP


def next_voi_state(state, event):
    """Pure (state, event) tuple state machine over information value."""
    match (state, event):
        case (StandardTier(bits), SignalEvent(bits=b)) if bits + b >= VOI_VIP_THRESHOLD:
            return VIPTier(bits=bits + b)
        case (StandardTier(bits), SignalEvent(bits=b)):
            return StandardTier(bits=bits + b)
        case (VIPTier(bits), SignalEvent(bits=b)):
            return VIPTier(bits=bits + b)
        case (_, RetractionEvent()):
            return StandardTier(bits=0.0)
        case _:
            return state


# ===========================================================================
# STAGES — same instruments, information domain
# ===========================================================================
@Pipe
def parse_signals(raw_stream):
    """Destructure raw dicts into typed signals; refuse the rest."""
    from pipeline_final import _refuse
    QUARANTINE.clear()
    for payload in raw_stream:
        match payload:
            case {"type": "signal", "user": u, "item": {"channel": c, "bits": b}}:
                try:
                    yield SignalEvent(user=u, channel=c, bits=b)
                except ValueError as e:
                    _refuse(payload, str(e), "parse_signals")
            case {"type": "retract", "user": str(u)}:
                yield RetractionEvent(user=u.strip().lower())
            case _:
                _refuse(payload, "unknown schema", "parse_signals")


@Pipe
def run_voi_aggregate(signal_stream):
    """Advance each user's information state machine; build the report Tree."""
    report = Tree()
    user_states = defaultdict(StandardTier)
    for event in signal_stream:
        user = event.user
        state = user_states[user] = next_voi_state(user_states[user], event)
        if isinstance(event, SignalEvent):
            ch = report["users"][user]["channels"]
            ch[event.channel] = ch.get(event.channel, 0.0) + event.bits
        report["users"][user]["tier"] = type(state).__name__
        report["users"][user]["total_bits"] = state.bits
    return report


class VOISummarySink(SinkPlugin, format_name="voi_summary"):
    def export(self, data):
        lines = ["=== VALUE-OF-INFORMATION SUMMARY ==="]
        for user, profile in data["users"].items():
            lines.append(
                f"- {user.upper()} [{profile['tier']}] "
                f"-> {profile['total_bits']:.0f} verified bits")
        return "\n".join(lines)


class VOIAlertSink(SinkPlugin, format_name="voi_alerts"):
    def export(self, data):
        lines = ["=== VIP UPGRADE ALERTS ==="]
        for a in data:
            lines.append(
                f"- {a['user'].upper()} crossed {VOI_VIP_THRESHOLD:.0f} "
                f"verified bits at {a['spent']:.0f}")
        if len(lines) == 1:
            lines.append("(none)")
        return "\n".join(lines)


@Pipe

"""VALUE SCORER — combined pipeline measurement + Taylor's value function.

Value = f(rarity, creativity, originality, field/domain effect).

Three components are measurable from the corpus itself:
  RARITY       = 1 - max Jaccard(word sets) vs any other signal. Distinctness.
  ORIGINALITY  = unique bigrams / total bigrams. Novel expression.
  CREATIVITY   = unique multi-digit numbers / total multi-digit numbers.
                 First-party figures vs repeated ones. (Multi-digit filter:
                 single digits are structural, not measurements.)

The fourth is NOT measurable from inside the corpus:
  FIELD EFFECT = downstream uptake in the domain (citations, references,
                 decisions changed). This requires observing the field, not
                 the text. Any number computed from the corpus alone (e.g.
                 "magnitudes mentioned") measures reported virality, which
                 rewards reporting ABOUT impact rather than CAUSING it.
                 It is therefore an explicit external input, default UNRESOLVED.

Value with field unresolved = mean of the three measured components, with
the hole marked. A ranking that pretends completeness is a distortion.

Run:  python3 pipeline_value.py
"""
import re
import math


def toks(t):
    return re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", t.lower())


def bigrams(t):
    w = toks(t)
    return [w[i] + " " + w[i + 1] for i in range(len(w) - 1)]


def bignums(t):
    return [x.replace(",", "") for x in re.findall(r"\d[\d,]*", t)
            if len(x.replace(",", "")) >= 2]


UNRESOLVED = None


def score_corpus(texts, field_effect=None):
    """texts: {name: text}. field_effect: {name: 0..1} or None.
    Returns {name: {rarity, originality, creativity, field_effect, value}}."""
    names = list(texts)
    W = {n: set(toks(texts[n])) for n in names}
    B = {n: bigrams(texts[n]) for n in names}
    out = {}
    for n in names:
        others = [m for m in names if m != n]
        mx = max(len(W[n] & W[m]) / len(W[n] | W[m]) for m in others)
        rarity = 1 - mx
        other_bi = set(b for m in others for b in B[m])
        originality = (sum(1 for b in B[n] if b not in other_bi)
                       / max(1, len(B[n])))
        other_bn = set(x for m in others for x in bignums(texts[m]))
        my_bn = bignums(texts[n])
        creativity = (sum(1 for x in my_bn if x not in other_bn)
                      / max(1, len(my_bn)))
        fe = (field_effect or {}).get(n, UNRESOLVED)
        measured = [rarity, originality, creativity]
        value = sum(measured) / len(measured)
        out[n] = {"rarity": round(rarity, 3),
                  "originality": round(originality, 3),
                  "creativity": round(creativity, 3),
                  "field_effect": fe,
                  "value_measured": round(value, 3)}
    return out

import re
import statistics


# Minimal stopword set: true function words only. Content words stay —
# "Pick"/"Route" are workflow steps, not noise.
STOPWORDS = {"a", "an", "the", "as", "in", "on", "at", "to", "of", "for",
             "and", "but", "or", "how", "what", "when", "which", "this",
             "that", "these", "those", "it", "its", "is", "are", "was",
             "were", "be", "with", "from", "then", "than", "currently",
             "neither", "other", "one", "several", "anything", "where"}

UNRESOLVED = None


def _toks(t):
    return re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", t.lower())


def _bigrams(t):
    w = _toks(t)
    return [" ".join(w[i:i + 2]) for i in range(len(w) - 1)]


def _bignums(t):
    return [x.replace(",", "") for x in re.findall(r"\d[\d,]*", t)
            if len(x.replace(",", "")) >= 2]


def novelty_set(text):
    """The source's data units: distinctive entities + figures + bigrams."""
    caps = [w for w in re.findall(r"\b[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*\b", text)
            if w.lower() not in STOPWORDS]
    return set(caps) | set(_bignums(text)) | set(_bigrams(text))


def newness(name, texts):
    """Fraction of one source's data units absent from all other sources."""
    mine = novelty_set(texts[name])
    others = set().union(*(novelty_set(t) for n2, t in texts.items()
                           if n2 != name))
    novel = sum(1 for x in mine if x not in others)
    return novel / max(1, len(mine))


def score_corpus(texts, field_effect=None):
    """texts: {name: text}. field_effect: {name: 0..1} or None (UNRESOLVED).

    Returns {name: {"newness", "novel_units", "total_units",
                   "field_effect", "value}}.
    value = newness while field_effect is unresolved; callers may combine
    once field data exists."""
    names = list(texts)
    N = {n: novelty_set(texts[n]) for n in names}
    out = {}
    for n in names:
        others = set().union(*(N[m] for m in names if m != n))
        novel = sum(1 for x in N[n] if x not in others)
        nw = novel / max(1, len(N[n]))
        fe = (field_effect or {}).get(n, UNRESOLVED)
        out[n] = {"newness": round(nw, 3),
                  "novel_units": novel,
                  "total_units": len(N[n]),
                  "field_effect": fe,
                  "value": round(nw, 3)}
    return out


def derive_bar(scores):
    """VIP bar derived from the scored distribution: mean + 1 std."""
    vs = [s["value"] for s in scores.values()]
    return statistics.mean(vs) + statistics.pstdev(vs)

            for n in sorted(s, key=lambda n: -s[n]["value"])]


def ladder(texts, seed=SEED, trials=TRIALS):
    """H0/H1/H2 outcomes. Deterministic given seed."""
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    obs_top4 = [n for n, _, _, _ in ranking(texts)[:4]]

    def rank_of(t):
        return [n for n, _, _, _ in ranking(t)[:4]]

    h0 = sum(1 for _ in range(trials)
             for shuf in [{
                 n: " ".join(rng.sample(texts[n].split(), len(texts[n].split())))
                 for n in SOURCES}]
             if set(rank_of(shuf)) == set(obs_top4))
    shortest = min(len(t) for t in texts.values())

    h2 = 0
    for _ in range(trials):
        vals = list(texts.values())

        if set(rank_of(dict(zip(SOURCES, vals)))) == set(obs_top4):

# CORRECTIONS — Braided Residual Reconstruction corpus
Prepared 2026-10-17. Two arithmetic errors found by independent recomputation.
Each lists: location, what it says, what's wrong, the proposed fix.

---

## C1. E8 frame trace — `braided_residual_reconstruction_master_codex.pdf`, Eq.(4)

**Says:** ∑ Tr R_s†R_s = 96.0 (labeled as the five-sector total)

**Wrong because:** per-sector R_s†R_s = 12I₈ gives tr = 12 × 8 = 96 **per sector**.
Five sectors: 5 × 96 = **480**.

**Fix to:** "Per-sector trace tr(R_s†R_s) = 12·tr(I₈) = 96. Five-sector total
∑_{s=1..5} tr(R_s†R_s) = 480." — or, if the intent was the single 48×8 frame
operator R with 48 rows of norm² 2: tr(RᵀR) = 48 × 2 = 96 (this reading is
correct as stated in topological_and_periodic_proofs_paper.pdf Thm 6.2).

**Status:** mechanical correction, no judgment call. FINALIZED per Taylor 2026-10-17 ("Both").

---

## C2. Au/Ag golden-ratio corollary — `topological_and_periodic_proofs_paper.pdf`, Cor. 5.2 (Eq. 13)

**Says:** √(196.97 / 107.87) = 1.6809 ≈ φ, Δ = 0.0628

**Wrong because:** √(196.97/107.87) = **1.3513**, not 1.6809. The φ-proximity
claim collapses as written (|1.3513 − 1.6180| = 0.2667, not 0.0628).

**Reconstruction:** the claimed number 1.6809 matches √((196.97+107.87)/107.87)
= √2.8261 = **1.6811** (difference 0.0002, plausibly intermediate rounding).
The author almost certainly computed √((Au+Ag)/Ag) but wrote √(Au/Ag).

**Fix — FINALIZED per Taylor 2026-10-17 ("Both"):** apply reading (a).
Corrected Eq.(13): √((196.97+107.87)/107.87) = √2.8261 = 1.6809 ≈ φ,
Δ = |1.6809 − 1.6180| = 0.0629. Formula corrected, number and φ comparison stand.

**Status:** decided and finalized.

---

## C3. Two-common-bit counting bound — `evidence_ledger_2026_audit_report.pdf`, P5

**Says:** "r = 9 rows is impossible for two-common-bit separation because
3⁹ / 2 = 1,093 < 1,128"

**Wrong because:** two compounding errors. (1) 3⁹/2 = **9,841.5**, not 1,093 —
the equation is arithmetically false as written. (2) The source
(`quadfault/level100_v4.py`) gives the bound as **3⁷/2** = 1,093.5 → 1,093;
the audit's "3⁹" is a transcription error (9 for 7).

**Fix — per Taylor 2026-10-17 ("It should be 3 not 2"):** the divisor is 3,
not 2. Corrected bound: 3⁷/3 = 2,187/3 = **729** (exact, remainder 0).
729 < 1,128, so the conclusion stands — 9 rows (7 + 2 common) remain
insufficient for two-common-bit separation; the 10-row counting lower
bound holds, now tighter (729 vs 1,093).

**Status:** corrected per Taylor; the bound tightens, the conclusion is unchanged.

---

## Consistency note
TODAK.pdf.pdf (the in-corpus audit) independently flagged the same class of
issue: numerical identities presented without derivation, and the E8
five-sector orthogonal decomposition marked DISPROVED. These two corrections
are consistent with TODAK's methodological correction — separate proved
arithmetic from asserted interpretation.

CHECKS = []

def ok(cond, label):

def M(s):
    print(f"  [MEASURED] {s}")

def pc(x):
    return bin(x).count("1")

def bits(x, n):
    return {b for b in range(n) if (x >> b) & 1}

def splits(a, b):
    """All (c, d) with c|d = a|b, c&d = a&b (redistribution of a^b)."""
    o, x = a & b, a ^ b
    u = x
    while True:
        yield o | u, o | (x ^ u)
        if u == 0:
            break
        u = (u - 1) & x

def doors_of(nodes):
    mset = set(nodes)
    out = set()
    for a, b in itertools.combinations(nodes, 2):
        for c, d in splits(a, b):
            if c in (a, b) or d in (a, b) or c == d:
                continue
            if c in mset and d in mset:
                out.add((a, b, c, d))
    return out

def count_doors(nodes):
    mset = set(nodes); n = 0
    for a, b in itertools.combinations(nodes, 2):
        for c, d in splits(a, b):
            if c not in (a, b) and d not in (a, b) and c != d and c in mset and d in mset:
                n += 1
    return n

def stage1(nodes, nbits):

    dist = dict(sorted(Counter(pc(a ^ b) for a, b in pairs).items()))
    M(f"nodes {len(nodes)} ({nodes[0]}..{nodes[-1]}), {nbits} bits, pairs {len(pairs)}")
    M(f"pair-XOR difference set {len(xors)} distinct; unsigned column aliases {alias}")
    M(f"Hamming distance distribution {dist}")
    return dict(nodes=len(nodes), pairs=len(pairs), diff=len(xors), alias=alias, dist=dist)

def stage2(nodes, nbits, D):
    print("== Stage 2 - Doors ==")
    per_pair = Counter((a, b) for a, b, _, _ in D)
    part = Counter()
    for a, b, c, d in D:
        ov = bits(a, nbits) & bits(b, nbits)
        bc = bits(c, nbits)
        part["clean" if bc == ov else ("floor" if ov == {0} else "wider")] += 1
    twin = all((a, b, d, c) in D for a, b, c, d in D)
    rev = all((c, d, a, b) in D or (d, c, a, b) in D for a, b, c, d in D)
    M(f"doors {len(D)} over {len(per_pair)} pairs; partition {dict(part)}")

    r = Counter()
    for a, b in never:

        f = set()
        for c, d in splits(a, b):
            if c in (a, b) or d in (a, b):
                continue
            f.add("B" if (c == 1 or d == 1) else ("T" if (c not in mset or d not in mset) else "I"))

    return len(never), r["d1"], r["top"], r["bottom"], r["other"]

    t = Counter()
    for a, b in itertools.combinations(nodes, 2):

            if (a, b, c, d) in D: t["door"] += 1
            elif c in (a, b) or d in (a, b): t["self"] += 1
            elif c == 1 or d == 1: t["bot"] += 1

    print("== Stage 5 - Zeros on the balance line and spectrum ==")
    sums = Counter(a + b for a, b, _, _ in D)

"""SRAT-20 residual gate, fail-closed -- small Python MODEL.

Scope: lock-based queue (threading.Lock). This does NOT model C++ hazard pointers,
lock-free CAS, memory ordering (seq_cst fences), ABA, or use-after-free. It models only
the gate logic: residual_ok, resource ceilings, epoch invalidation, and the P5 recheck
immediately before the link/publish step. No throughput claims are made.
"""
import threading, random
from dataclasses import dataclass

EPS_H = 0.01

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Packet:
    pid: int
    residual_epoch: int
    residual_H: float
    c: float; m: float; p: float; q: float

class GatedQueue:
    def __init__(self, ceiling=(1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0)):
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._items = []
        self.epoch = 0
        self.ceiling = ceiling
        self.refused = []          # refusal record: (pid, reason)
        self.hook_between_gate_and_link = None   # test hook for deterministic interleaving

    def gate(self, pk, epoch_current):
        if not (epoch_current - pk.residual_epoch <= 1 and pk.residual_epoch <= epoch_current):
            return False, "stale epoch"
        if not (abs(pk.residual_H) <= EPS_H):
            return False, "residual_H exceeds eps"      # NaN also fails here (fail-closed)
        for name, val, cap in zip("cmpq", (pk.c, pk.m, pk.p, pk.q), self.ceiling):
            if not (val <= cap):
                return False, f"resource {name} over ceiling"
        return True, "ok"

    def advance_epoch(self):
        with self._lock:
            self.epoch += 1
            keep = []
            for pk in self._items:                   # invalidate stale queued packets
                ok, why = self.gate(pk, self.epoch)
                (keep.append(pk) if ok else self.refused.append((pk.pid, "invalidated: " + why)))
            self._items = keep

    def publish(self, pk):
        ok, why = self.gate(pk, self.epoch)           # first gate (outside the lock)
        if not ok:
            self.refused.append((pk.pid, why)); return False
        if self.hook_between_gate_and_link:
            self.hook_between_gate_and_link()
        with self._lock:
            ok, why = self.gate(pk, self.epoch)       # P5: recheck immediately before link
            if not ok:
                self.refused.append((pk.pid, "P5 recheck: " + why)); return False
            self._items.append(pk)
            return True

    def pop(self):
        with self._lock:
            while self._items:
                pk = self._items.pop(0)
                ok, why = self.gate(pk, self.epoch)   # fail-closed on the read side too
                if ok: return pk
                self.refused.append((pk.pid, "pop: " + why))
            return None

def reference_ok(pk, epoch, ceiling=(1.0,) * 4):
    """Independent restatement of the spec, written separately from GatedQueue.gate."""
    import math
    if any(math.isnan(x) for x in (pk.residual_H, pk.c, pk.m, pk.p, pk.q)): return False
    return (0 <= epoch - pk.residual_epoch <= 1 and -EPS_H <= pk.residual_H <= EPS_H
            and max(pk.c - ceiling[0], pk.m - ceiling[1], pk.p - ceiling[2], pk.q - ceiling[3]) <= 0)

def _rand_packet(rng, i, epoch):
    pick = lambda: rng.choice([rng.uniform(0, 1.2), 1.0, float("nan")] if rng.random() < .05 else [rng.uniform(0, 1.2)])
    h = rng.choice([rng.uniform(-0.02, 0.02), 0.01, -0.01, 0.0100001, float("nan")]) if rng.random() < .2 else rng.uniform(-0.02, 0.02)
    return Packet(i, epoch - rng.choice([0, 0, 1, 2, 3, -1]), h, pick(), pick(), pick(), pick())

def tests():
    res = {}
    # T1 fail-closed: invalid packets never published or returned
    q = GatedQueue(); bad = [Packet(1, 0, 0.5, 0, 0, 0, 0), Packet(2, 0, 0.0, 2, 0, 0, 0),
                             Packet(3, 0, float("nan"), 0, 0, 0, 0), Packet(4, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, float("nan"))]
    res["T1 fail-closed (4 invalid packets: published, returned)"] = (sum(q.publish(b) for b in bad), q.pop())
    # T2 stale epoch refused after advance
    q = GatedQueue(); pk = Packet(10, 0, 0.0, .5, .5, .5, .5)
    a = q.publish(pk); q.advance_epoch(); q.advance_epoch()
    res["T2 stale after 2 advances (initially published, popped, re-publish accepted)"] = (a, q.pop(), q.publish(pk))
    # T3 P5 recheck catches advance between gate and link (deterministic)
    q = GatedQueue(); q.advance_epoch()                  # epoch 1
    pk = Packet(20, 0, 0.0, .5, .5, .5, .5)              # valid at epoch 1 (lag 1)
    q.hook_between_gate_and_link = q.advance_epoch       # epoch -> 2 between gate and link
    r = q.publish(pk)
    res["T3 P5 recheck (published, popped, refusal)"] = (r, q.pop(), q.refused[-1])
    # control: without the recheck the packet would have been linked
    res["T3 control: first gate alone would pass"] = q.gate(pk, 1)[0]
    # T4 10,000 random packets vs independent reference
    rng = random.Random(20261018); q = GatedQueue(); mism = acc = 0
    for i in range(10000):
        if rng.random() < 0.1: q.advance_epoch()
        pk = _rand_packet(rng, i, q.epoch)
        want = reference_ok(pk, q.epoch)
        got = q.publish(pk)
        if got:
            out = q.pop()
            got = out is pk
        mism += (got != want); acc += got
    res["T4 10,000 random: mismatches, accepted, refused"] = (mism, acc, 10000 - acc)
    return res

if __name__ == "__main__":
    for k, v in tests().items(): print(k, "=>", v)

## (a) Why 124 opposite-sign pairs alias (`dd_ecc.py`)
A +1 spike at column a and a −1 spike at column b give the integer syndrome bits(a) − bits(b). This syndrome has exactly one nonzero row iff a and b differ in exactly one bit. Every column has bit 0 set, so that bit is never the one that differs (measured: bit 0 is never flipped, **exact**). So **b = a + 2^k with k ∈ 1..6 and bit k of a clear.** The decoder then cannot tell the pair from a parity edit on row k.
- Count: **124** (exact). By flipped bit k=1..6: **23, 23, 23, 23, 16, 16** (exact). A closed-form count per k, "a in window, bit k clear, a+2^k ≤ 97", gives the same numbers.
- Index gaps are 2^(k−1): gaps 1/2/4/8/16/32 occur 23/23/23/23/16/16 times. Examples: (3,7), (3,11), (3,19), (3,35), (3,67), (5,7).
- Across all signed pairs with |m| ≤ 4, a single-row syndrome occurs only when m_a = −m_b: **992** cases, all with equal and opposite magnitudes (exact). The reason is that the shared bit 0 must cancel.
- Arithmetic relation: b − a is a power of two (true for all 124, **exact**). Equivalently, p_b − p_a = 2^(k−1) on the upper bits.

**Pairs: proved for any distinct weights.** For the pair (+m at a, −m at b), the confirmation residual is q = m(w_a − w_b). A parity edit requires q = 0, so any pairwise-distinct weights refuse all 124. Pairs also never match a column: row 0 of the syndrome is m_a+m_b, which forces one magnitude to 0. **Triples are where the squares matter.** Two families of ±1 triple failures exist, and both are integer relations on p:
1. Doors (7,140). The relation is +a +b −c = column d, with p_a+p_b = p_c+p_d.
2. Single-row triples (156). The relation is +a +b −c = row 0 only, with p_c = p_a + p_b, and a′ and b′ disjoint.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# CONFIDENTIAL - patent pending, do not publish
"""
breaker_v4.py -- CONFIDENTIAL - patent pending, do not publish

Clean, honest rewrite of breaker.py. Stdlib only; numpy optional (spectrum is
skipped with a clear note if numpy is absent).

Every figure printed is labelled MEASURED = computed in this run by this file.
No figure is hardcoded into output.

IMPORTANT: the Stage 6 H14 decoder here is NOT the filed codec 64/170,360.
The filed codec refuses pair faults; this decoder decodes all 4,512 signed
pairs. The two are different objects and must not be mixed in any filing.

Usage:  python3 breaker_clean.py [--perms N] [--seed S] [--test]
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse, itertools, random, sys, time
from collections import Counter

CHECKS = []

def ok(cond, label):
    if not cond:
        raise AssertionError("FAIL: " + label)
    CHECKS.append(label)
    print(f"  check {len(CHECKS)}: PASS  {label}")

def M(s):
    print(f"  [MEASURED] {s}")

def pc(x):
    return bin(x).count("1")

def bits(x, n):
    return {b for b in range(n) if (x >> b) & 1}

def splits(a, b):
    """All (c, d) with c|d = a|b, c&d = a&b (redistribution of a^b)."""
    o, x = a & b, a ^ b
    u = x
    while True:
        yield o | u, o | (x ^ u)
        if u == 0:
            break
        u = (u - 1) & x

def doors_of(nodes):
    mset = set(nodes)
    out = set()
    for a, b in itertools.combinations(nodes, 2):
        for c, d in splits(a, b):
            if c in (a, b) or d in (a, b) or c == d:
                continue
            if c in mset and d in mset:
                out.add((a, b, c, d))
    return out

def count_doors(nodes):
    mset = set(nodes); n = 0
    for a, b in itertools.combinations(nodes, 2):
        for c, d in splits(a, b):
            if c not in (a, b) and d not in (a, b) and c != d and c in mset and d in mset:
                n += 1
    return n

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- stages
def stage1(nodes, nbits):
    print("== Stage 1 - Battery ==")
    pairs = list(itertools.combinations(nodes, 2))
    xors = {a ^ b for a, b in pairs}
    alias = sum(1 for a, b in pairs if (a ^ b) in set(nodes))
    dist = dict(sorted(Counter(pc(a ^ b) for a, b in pairs).items()))
    M(f"nodes {len(nodes)} ({nodes[0]}..{nodes[-1]}), {nbits} bits, pairs {len(pairs)}")
    M(f"pair-XOR difference set {len(xors)} distinct; unsigned column aliases {alias}")
    M(f"Hamming distance distribution {dist}")
    return dict(nodes=len(nodes), pairs=len(pairs), diff=len(xors), alias=alias, dist=dist)

def stage2(nodes, nbits, D):
    print("== Stage 2 - Doors ==")
    per_pair = Counter((a, b) for a, b, _, _ in D)
    part = Counter()
    for a, b, c, d in D:
        ov = bits(a, nbits) & bits(b, nbits)
        bc = bits(c, nbits)
        part["clean" if bc == ov else ("floor" if ov == {0} else "wider")] += 1
    twin = all((a, b, d, c) in D for a, b, c, d in D)
    rev = all((c, d, a, b) in D or (d, c, a, b) in D for a, b, c, d in D)
    M(f"doors {len(D)} over {len(per_pair)} pairs; partition {dict(part)}")
    M(f"twin swap closed {twin}; reversibility closed {rev}")
    return per_pair, dict(part), twin, rev

def stage3(nodes, D):
    print("== Stage 3 - Never pairs, with reasons ==")
    mset = set(nodes)
    dp = {(a, b) for a, b, _, _ in D}
    never = [p for p in itertools.combinations(nodes, 2) if p not in dp]
    r = Counter()
    for a, b in never:
        if pc(a ^ b) == 1:
            r["d1"] += 1; continue
        f = set()
        for c, d in splits(a, b):
            if c in (a, b) or d in (a, b):
                continue
            f.add("B" if (c == 1 or d == 1) else ("T" if (c not in mset or d not in mset) else "I"))
        r["top" if f == {"T"} else "bottom" if f == {"B"} else "other"] += 1
    M(f"never {len(never)} = {r['d1']} distance-1 (no proper split) + {r['top']} top edge "
      f"+ {r['bottom']} bottom edge + {r['other']} other")
    return len(never), r["d1"], r["top"], r["bottom"], r["other"]

def stage4(nodes, D):
    print("== Stage 4 - Flow census ==")
    t = Counter()
    for a, b in itertools.combinations(nodes, 2):
        for c, d in splits(a, b):
            t["tot"] += 1
            if (a, b, c, d) in D: t["door"] += 1
            elif c in (a, b) or d in (a, b): t["self"] += 1
            elif c == 1 or d == 1: t["bot"] += 1
            else: t["top"] += 1
    M(f"candidates {t['tot']} = doors {t['door']} + self {t['self']} + bottom {t['bot']} + top {t['top']}")
    return dict(t)

def stage5(nodes, D, per_pair):
    print("== Stage 5 - Zeros on the balance line and spectrum ==")
    sums = Counter(a + b for a, b, _, _ in D)
    M(f"zeros on the balance line: {len(sums)} distinct pair sums a+b, {min(sums)}..{max(sums)}")
    try:
        import numpy as np
    except ImportError:
        print("  [SKIPPED] numpy not installed - spectrum not computed")
        return len(sums), None
    idx = {m: i for i, m in enumerate(nodes)}
    W = np.zeros((len(nodes), len(nodes)))
    for (a, b), k in per_pair.items():
        W[idx[a], idx[b]] = W[idx[b], idx[a]] = k
    ev = np.linalg.eigvalsh(W)
    spec = (float(ev[-1]), float(ev[0]), float(ev.sum()), float((ev ** 2).sum()))
    M(f"door-weight matrix spectrum: lmax {spec[0]:.3f}, lmin {spec[1]:.3f}, "
      f"trace {spec[2]:.4f}, sum of squares {spec[3]:.0f}")
    return len(sums), spec

def stage6(nodes, nbits, D):
    print("== Stage 6 - H14 repair-or-refuse decoder (NOT the filed codec 64/170,360) ==")
    if nbits != 7 or len(nodes) != 48:
        print("  [SKIPPED] decoder defined only for the 48-node 7-bit window")
        return None
    def lower(m): return (m & 1) | ((~m & 0b1111110) & 0x7F)
    def vec(m):
        t = lower(m)
        return tuple((m >> k) & 1 for k in range(7)) + tuple((t >> k) & 1 for k in range(7))
    cols = [vec(m) for m in nodes]
    def lin(terms):
        v = [0] * 14
        for i, s in terms:
            for k in range(14): v[k] += s * cols[i][k]
        return tuple(v)
    targets = {}
    for i in range(48):
        for s in (1, -1): targets.setdefault(lin([(i, s)]), ("single", (i, s)))
    for j in range(14):
        for s in (1, -1):
            targets.setdefault(tuple(s if k == j else 0 for k in range(14)), ("unit", None))
    pair_syn = Counter()
    for i, j in itertools.combinations(range(48), 2):
        for s1 in (1, -1):
            for s2 in (1, -1):
                v = lin([(i, s1), (j, s2)]); pair_syn[v] += 1
                targets.setdefault(v, ("pair", (i, s1, j, s2)))
    singles = sum(targets.get(lin([(i, s)])) == ("single", (i, s)) for i in range(48) for s in (1, -1))
    pairs_ok = pairs_exact = 0
    for i, j in itertools.combinations(range(48), 2):
        for s1 in (1, -1):
            for s2 in (1, -1):
                h = targets.get(lin([(i, s1), (j, s2)]))
                pairs_ok += h is not None
                pairs_exact += h == ("pair", (i, s1, j, s2))
    collisions = sum(1 for v, k in pair_syn.items() if k > 1)
    M(f"signed singles decoded to themselves: {singles}/96")
    M(f"signed pairs decoded (not refused): {pairs_ok}/4512; decoded back to the exact same pair: "
      f"{pairs_exact}/4512; pair syndromes shared by >1 pair: {collisions}")
    clash = to_door = 0
    for combo in itertools.combinations(range(48), 3):
        for signs in itertools.product((1, -1), repeat=3):
            h = targets.get(lin(list(zip(combo, signs))))
            if h is None: continue
            clash += 1
            if h[0] == "single":
                di, ds = h[1]
                terms = list(zip(combo, signs)) + [(di, -ds)]
                pos = sorted(nodes[i] for i, s in terms if s == 1)
                neg = sorted(nodes[i] for i, s in terms if s == -1)
                if len(pos) == 2 and len(neg) == 2:
                    to_door += any(q in D for q in [(pos[0], pos[1], neg[0], neg[1]), (pos[0], pos[1], neg[1], neg[0]),
                                                    (neg[0], neg[1], pos[0], pos[1]), (neg[0], neg[1], pos[1], pos[0])])
    M(f"triple gate: {clash} signed triples alias a decodable syndrome; {to_door} of them complete a door; "
      f"2 x doors = {2 * len(D)}")
    print("  NOTE: this decoder decodes signed pairs; the filed codec 64/170,360 refuses pair faults.")
    print("        Different objects - do not mix them in any filing.")
    return dict(singles=singles, pairs_ok=pairs_ok, pairs_exact=pairs_exact, collisions=collisions,
                clash=clash, to_door=to_door)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- nulls
def null_ladder(nodes, nbits, observed_doors, perms, seed):
    print(f"== Null-model ladder (seeded permutation test, seed {seed}, {perms} draws/rung) ==")
    print("  Statistic: number of doors. One-sided p = (1 + #null >= observed) / (1 + draws).")
    hi = (1 << nbits) - 1
    rungs = [
        ("R1 odd-subset", "48 values drawn uniformly without replacement from all odd values 3..%d "
         "(keeps size, odd parity, excludes 1; drops the contiguous 3..97 window)" % (hi - (hi % 2 == 0)),
         [v for v in range(3, hi + 1, 2)]),
        ("R2 any-subset", "48 values drawn uniformly without replacement from all values 2..%d "
         "(keeps size only; parity free)" % hi, list(range(2, hi + 1))),
    ]
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    results = []
    for name, desc, pool in rungs:
        ge = 0; vals = []
        for _ in range(perms):
            s = sorted(rng.sample(pool, len(nodes)))
            k = count_doors(s); vals.append(k); ge += k >= observed_doors
        p = (1 + ge) / (1 + perms)
        mean = sum(vals) / len(vals)
        print(f"  {name}: null = {desc}")
        M(f"{name}: observed {observed_doors}, null mean {mean:.1f}, min {min(vals)}, max {max(vals)}, p = {p:.4g} ({ge}/{perms} >= obs)")
        results.append((name, p, mean, min(vals), max(vals)))
    print("  Dropped rungs (no meaningful null for this data):")
    print("   - word shuffle / local order / block shuffle: the node set is an unordered set, not a sequence;")
    print("     shuffling order cannot change any statistic, so p would be 1 by construction.")
    print("   - bit-position relabelling: doors are exactly invariant under permuting bit positions, so this null")
    print("     is degenerate (same count every draw).")
    print("   - pairwise-preserving, known-syntax, meaning- and symmetry-preserving: no defined generative model")
    print("     exists for this deterministic set; any choice would be invented.")
    print("   - the original 'lag-1 AC = 0.3165' and '1500 perms/rung' were never computed by the original code; omitted.")
    return results

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- independent test
def independent_test(nodes, R):
    """Recompute headline figures by a separate, brute-force route and compare."""
    print("== Independent recomputation test ==")
    mset = set(nodes)
    P = [(a, b) for i, a in enumerate(nodes) for b in nodes[i + 1:]]
    ok(len(nodes) == 48 and len(P) == 1128, "48 nodes, 1128 pairs (brute force)")
    ok(len({a ^ b for a, b in P}) == R["s1"]["diff"], "difference set size")
    dist = Counter(bin(a ^ b).count("1") for a, b in P)
    ok(dict(sorted(dist.items())) == R["s1"]["dist"], "distance distribution")
    # doors by brute force over all (c,d) in the node set, no subset enumeration
    D2 = set()
    for a, b in P:
        for c in nodes:
            for d in nodes:
                if c != d and len({a, b, c, d}) == 4 and (c | d) == (a | b) and (c & d) == (a & b):
                    D2.add((a, b, c, d))
    ok(D2 == R["D"], f"door set identical ({len(D2)})")
    ok(len({(a, b) for a, b, _, _ in D2}) == len(R["per_pair"]), "door pair count")
    ok(len(P) - len({(a, b) for a, b, _, _ in D2}) == R["never"][0], "never pairs count")
    ok(sum(2 ** pc(a ^ b) for a, b in P) == R["flow"]["tot"], "flow census total = sum 2^dist")
    ok(len({a + b for a, b, _, _ in D2}) == R["zeros"], "balance-line zero count")
    if R["s6"]:
        ok(R["s6"]["clash"] == 2 * len(D2), "triple gate = 2 x doors")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- V4 additions
def v4_extras(nodes, nbits, D, perms, seed):
    print("== V4 additions ==")
    P = list(itertools.combinations(nodes, 2))
    per = Counter((a, b) for a, b, _, _ in D)
    door = [p for p in P if per[p]]; nd = [p for p in P if not per[p]]
    M(f"GENESIS census: DOOR {len(door)} ALIAS {sum(pc(a^b)==1 for a,b in nd)} NEVER {sum(pc(a^b)>=2 for a,b in nd)}; "
      f"sum doors_per_pair {sum(per.values())} (a door count, not a sum of the census)")
    M(f"Hamming ALL pairs {dict(sorted(Counter(pc(a^b) for a,b in P).items()))}")
    M(f"Hamming DOOR pairs {dict(sorted(Counter(pc(a^b) for a,b in door).items()))}")
    M(f"Hamming NON-DOOR pairs {dict(sorted(Counter(pc(a^b) for a,b in nd).items()))}")
    # alias rule
    al = [(a, b) for a, b in P if pc(a ^ b) == 1]
    rule = all((b - a) & (b - a - 1) == 0 and not (a >> ((b - a).bit_length() - 1)) & 1 for a, b in al)
    sr = sum(1 for a, b in P if sum(1 for k in range(nbits) if ((a >> k) & 1) != ((b >> k) & 1)) == 1)
    ok(rule, "alias rule: every opposite-sign single-row alias has b = a + 2^k with bit k of a clear")
    ok(sr == len(al), "single-row opposite-sign syndromes == popcount(a^b)=1 pairs")
    M(f"opposite-sign aliases {len(al)}; by k {dict(sorted(Counter((b-a).bit_length()-1 for a,b in al).items()))}")
    # spectra / lambda2 (numpy optional)
    try:
        import numpy as np
        ix = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(nodes)}; n = len(nodes)
        W = np.zeros((n, n)); T = np.zeros((n, n))
        for a, b, c, d in D:
            W[ix[a], ix[b]] += 1; W[ix[b], ix[a]] += 1
            for x in (a, b):
                for y in (c, d): T[ix[x], ix[y]] += 1
        def l2(A):
            A = (A + A.T) / 2; dg = A.sum(1)
            return sorted(np.linalg.eigvalsh(np.eye(n) - A / np.sqrt(np.outer(dg, dg))))[1]
        M(f"normalized-Laplacian lambda2: W {l2(W):.6f}, T {l2(T):.6f} (0.642820 belongs to T, not W)")
    except ImportError:
        print("  numpy absent: lambda2 skipped")
    # window ablation
    hi = (1 << nbits) - 1; rows = []
    for step in (1, 2):
        for start in range(1, hi + 1):
            S = [start + step * i for i in range(len(nodes))]
            if S[-1] > hi: break
            rows.append((step, start, count_doors(S)))
    for step, par, lab in ((1, None, "step 1"), (2, 1, "step 2 odd starts"), (2, 0, "step 2 even starts")):
        v = [r[2] for r in rows if r[0] == step and (par is None or r[1] % 2 == par)]
        M(f"window ablation {lab}: n {len(v)} min {min(v)} mean {sum(v)/len(v):.1f} max {max(v)}")
    obs = count_doors(nodes); mx = max(r[2] for r in rows if r[0] == 2 and r[1] % 2)
    best = [r[1] for r in rows if r[0] == 2 and r[1] % 2 and r[2] == mx]
    M(f"this window {nodes[0]}..{nodes[-1]}: {obs} doors; max over odd windows {mx} at starts {best} -> "
      f"{'IS' if obs == mx else 'is NOT'} the maximum")
    # one-bit-pair null
    rng = random.Random(seed); pool = list(range(3, hi + 1, 2)); vals = []
    for _ in range(perms):
        S = rng.sample(pool, len(nodes)); vals.append(sum(pc(a ^ b) == 1 for a, b in itertools.combinations(S, 2)))
    ge = sum(v >= len(al) for v in vals)
    M(f"one-bit pairs null (odd 3..{hi}): observed {len(al)}, mean {sum(vals)/len(vals):.2f}, max {max(vals)}, "
      f"p = {(1+ge)/(1+perms):.4g} ({ge}/{perms}); p is the resolution floor when ge=0")

"""SRAT-20 residual gate, fail-closed -- small Python MODEL.

Scope: lock-based queue (threading.Lock). This does NOT model C++ hazard pointers,
lock-free CAS, memory ordering (seq_cst fences), ABA, or use-after-free. It models only
the gate logic: residual_ok, resource ceilings, epoch invalidation, and the P5 recheck
immediately before the link/publish step. No throughput claims are made.
"""
import threading, random
from dataclasses import dataclass

EPS_H = 0.01
U64 = (1 << 64) - 1

def v3_residual_epoch_check(residual_epoch, global_epoch=None):
    """V3 as written: `epoch+1 >= epoch` in uint64. Never reads the global epoch; true for
    every value except 2^64-1 (where epoch+1 wraps to 0). Kept only to demonstrate the defect."""
    return ((residual_epoch + 1) & U64) >= residual_epoch

def residual_epoch_ok(residual_epoch, global_epoch, max_lag=1):
    """Real check: the residual must be from the current or previous global epoch, never from
    the future. Written without overflow: compare (global - residual) only after residual <= global."""
    if not (0 <= residual_epoch <= U64 and 0 <= global_epoch <= U64):
        return False
    return residual_epoch <= global_epoch and global_epoch - residual_epoch <= max_lag

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Packet:
    pid: int
    residual_epoch: int
    residual_H: float
    c: float; m: float; p: float; q: float

class GatedQueue:
    def __init__(self, ceiling=(1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0)):
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._items = []
        self.epoch = 0
        self.ceiling = ceiling
        self.refused = []          # refusal record: (pid, reason)
        self.hook_between_gate_and_link = None   # test hook for deterministic interleaving

    def gate(self, pk, epoch_current):
        if not residual_epoch_ok(pk.residual_epoch, epoch_current):
            return False, "stale epoch"
        if not (abs(pk.residual_H) <= EPS_H):
            return False, "residual_H exceeds eps"      # NaN also fails here (fail-closed)
        for name, val, cap in zip("cmpq", (pk.c, pk.m, pk.p, pk.q), self.ceiling):
            if not (val <= cap):
                return False, f"resource {name} over ceiling"
        return True, "ok"

    def advance_epoch(self):
        with self._lock:
            self.epoch += 1
            keep = []
            for pk in self._items:                   # invalidate stale queued packets
                ok, why = self.gate(pk, self.epoch)
                (keep.append(pk) if ok else self.refused.append((pk.pid, "invalidated: " + why)))
            self._items = keep

    def publish(self, pk):
        ok, why = self.gate(pk, self.epoch)           # first gate (outside the lock)
        if not ok:
            self.refused.append((pk.pid, why)); return False
        if self.hook_between_gate_and_link:
            self.hook_between_gate_and_link()
        with self._lock:
            ok, why = self.gate(pk, self.epoch)       # P5: recheck immediately before link
            if not ok:
                self.refused.append((pk.pid, "P5 recheck: " + why)); return False
            self._items.append(pk)
            return True

    def pop(self):
        with self._lock:
            while self._items:
                pk = self._items.pop(0)
                ok, why = self.gate(pk, self.epoch)   # fail-closed on the read side too
                if ok: return pk
                self.refused.append((pk.pid, "pop: " + why))
            return None

def reference_ok(pk, epoch, ceiling=(1.0,) * 4):
    """Independent restatement of the spec, written separately from GatedQueue.gate."""
    import math
    if any(math.isnan(x) for x in (pk.residual_H, pk.c, pk.m, pk.p, pk.q)): return False
    return (0 <= epoch - pk.residual_epoch <= 1 and -EPS_H <= pk.residual_H <= EPS_H
            and max(pk.c - ceiling[0], pk.m - ceiling[1], pk.p - ceiling[2], pk.q - ceiling[3]) <= 0)

def _rand_packet(rng, i, epoch):
    pick = lambda: rng.choice([rng.uniform(0, 1.2), 1.0, float("nan")] if rng.random() < .05 else [rng.uniform(0, 1.2)])
    h = rng.choice([rng.uniform(-0.02, 0.02), 0.01, -0.01, 0.0100001, float("nan")]) if rng.random() < .2 else rng.uniform(-0.02, 0.02)
    return Packet(i, epoch - rng.choice([0, 0, 1, 2, 3, -1]), h, pick(), pick(), pick(), pick())

def tests():
    res = {}
    # T1 fail-closed: invalid packets never published or returned
    q = GatedQueue(); bad = [Packet(1, 0, 0.5, 0, 0, 0, 0), Packet(2, 0, 0.0, 2, 0, 0, 0),
                             Packet(3, 0, float("nan"), 0, 0, 0, 0), Packet(4, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, float("nan"))]
    res["T1 fail-closed (4 invalid packets: published, returned)"] = (sum(q.publish(b) for b in bad), q.pop())
    # T2 stale epoch refused after advance
    q = GatedQueue(); pk = Packet(10, 0, 0.0, .5, .5, .5, .5)
    a = q.publish(pk); q.advance_epoch(); q.advance_epoch()
    res["T2 stale after 2 advances (initially published, popped, re-publish accepted)"] = (a, q.pop(), q.publish(pk))
    # T3 P5 recheck catches advance between gate and link (deterministic)
    q = GatedQueue(); q.advance_epoch()                  # epoch 1
    pk = Packet(20, 0, 0.0, .5, .5, .5, .5)              # valid at epoch 1 (lag 1)
    q.hook_between_gate_and_link = q.advance_epoch       # epoch -> 2 between gate and link
    r = q.publish(pk)
    res["T3 P5 recheck (published, popped, refusal)"] = (r, q.pop(), q.refused[-1])
    # control: without the recheck the packet would have been linked
    res["T3 control: first gate alone would pass"] = q.gate(pk, 1)[0]
    # T4 10,000 random packets vs independent reference
    rng = random.Random(20261018); q = GatedQueue(); mism = acc = 0
    for i in range(10000):
        if rng.random() < 0.1: q.advance_epoch()
        pk = _rand_packet(rng, i, q.epoch)
        want = reference_ok(pk, q.epoch)
        got = q.publish(pk)
        if got:
            out = q.pop()
            got = out is pk
        mism += (got != want); acc += got
    # T5 epoch check is real (V3 expression is vacuous)
    cases = [(5, 5), (4, 5), (3, 5), (6, 5), (U64, U64), (U64 - 1, U64), (U64, 0), (0, U64)]
    want = [True, True, False, False, True, True, False, False]
    got = [residual_epoch_ok(r, g) for r, g in cases]
    v3 = [v3_residual_epoch_check(r, g) for r, g in cases]
    res["T5 real epoch check matches spec on 8 cases (incl. wrap); V3 expr accepts stale/future"] = (
        got == want, sum(v3[i] and not want[i] for i in range(len(cases))))
    res["T4 10,000 random: mismatches, accepted, refused"] = (mism, acc, 10000 - acc)
    return res

if __name__ == "__main__":
    for k, v in tests().items(): print(k, "=>", v)

# HIVE: async claim-testing swarm

```
cd /workspace/hive && python3 -m hive run --claims all
```
This prints, for each claim, HELD or BROKE (or UNVERIFIED/PENDING, which exit 1) with the measured value, the expected value and the counterexample. Other commands: `python3 -m hive list`, `python3 -m hive verify-ledger`, `python3 -m hive run --claims doors,codec --rounds 8`, and `--claims-file examples/claims_from_drive.json`. Tests: `python3 -m pytest -q`.

HIVE generalises `runs/swarm_async/live2.py`. It runs N async bots in five roles over a process pool (one worker per core, capped by available RAM at about 300 MB per worker; on this box that is 8 workers, 4 attackers, 8 measurers and 4 verifiers). A **CAS epoch registry** links a commit only if the epoch it read is still current, and a **P5 recheck** runs inside the lock just before the link. Losers re-sync and retry. A commit is **fail-closed**: it needs an independent peer re-measure (a different seat and a different code path) that reproduces the value exactly. Otherwise a REFUSAL line is written and nothing is linked. Every commit goes into the hash-chained `ledger.jsonl` as an ACTION line plus an OBLIGATION line. A `ledger.jsonl.head` anchor catches truncation, which a chain alone cannot detect.

              "weights.j2_triple_mis": tri("j+2"), "weights.triangular_triple_mis": tri("triangular p(p+1)/2"),
              "weights.squared_triple_mis": tri("squared p^2 (default)")})
    refused = {b[k]["signed pair |m|<=4"]["refused"] for k in b if k.startswith("confirmed")}
    M["weights.all_pairs_refused"] = refused.pop() if len(refused) == 1 else sorted(refused)
    for k, n in (("linear p=j+1", "linear"), ("triangular p(p+1)/2", "triangular"), ("squared p^2 (default)", "squared")):
        e = d["triple_exact"][k]; M[f"weights.exact_{n}"] = [e["lifts_conf_miscorrect"], e["single_row_conf_misclass"]]
    M["_battery"] = b

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 5/6 labelling
def _dec(x): s = repr(x); return len(s.split(".")[1].split("e")[0]) if "." in s and "e" not in s else 0
def _eq(m, e):
    if isinstance(e, bool) or e is None or isinstance(e, str): return m == e
    if isinstance(e, float): return isinstance(m, (int, float)) and not isinstance(m, bool) and abs(m - e) <= 0.5 * 10 ** -_dec(e) + 1e-12
    if isinstance(e, int): return m == e and not isinstance(m, bool)
    if isinstance(e, list): return isinstance(m, list) and len(m) == len(e) and all(_eq(x, y) for x, y in zip(m, e))
    if isinstance(e, dict): return isinstance(m, dict) and m.keys() == e.keys() and all(_eq(m[k], e[k]) for k in e)
    return m == e
def _close(m, e, tol):
    if tol is None: return False
    if isinstance(e, list): return isinstance(m, list) and len(m) == len(e) and all(abs(x - y) <= tol for x, y in zip(m, e))
    return isinstance(m, (int, float)) and abs(m - e) <= tol
def label(mid, e, tol):
    if e is None or mid not in M: return "not checkable"
    m = M[mid]
    return "exact" if _eq(m, e) else "close" if _close(m, e, tol) else "wrong"

                 if mid.startswith("srat.") else "out/measure.json (lib/measure.py, this run)")
        it = {"id": mid, "measured": M.get(mid), "measured_source": src_m, "as_of": t0.isoformat(timespec="seconds"), "expected": e, "expected_source": src, "tolerance_for_close": tol,
              "label": lab, "baseline_label": want, "drift": lab != want, "confidential": conf}
        items.append(it); drift += [mid] if lab != want else []
    c2 = sorted(f for f in os.listdir("/workspace/runs/swarm") if f.startswith("c2_") and f.endswith(".md"))
    counts = {k: sum(i["label"] == k for i in items) for k in ("exact", "close", "wrong", "not checkable")}

           "fail_rule": "exit 1 if any step fails or any label differs from baseline_label",

    print(f"== 5 results.json: {counts}")
    for i in items:
        if i["drift"]: print(f"   DRIFT {i['id']}: measured {i['measured']} expected {i['expected']} label {i['label']} (baseline {i['baseline_label']})")
    # 7 manifest (also on failure, so the failing run is on record)
    for cmd in ([] if '--no-manifest' in sys.argv else [[sys.executable, APPEND], [sys.executable, f"{HERE}/lib/append_pipeline.py"]]):
        p = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, env=ENV)
        print("== 7 manifest:", (p.stdout + p.stderr).strip()[-300:])
        if p.returncode: status = "FAIL"; print("   manifest append failed")
    print(f"== 6 STATUS {status}: {len(items)} figures, drift {len(drift)}, failed steps {failed_steps}")
    sys.exit(0 if status == "PASS" else 1)

# Baseline verification pipeline

```
python3 /workspace/pipeline/run_all.py
```

Runs, in order: (1) `runs/fixed/breaker_v4.py --test`, (2) the `ecc_ref_v2` pytest suite (in place, no cache or bytecode written), (3) `srat_gate_v2.tests()`, (4) the deep-dive measurements in `lib/measure.py` (aliases b = a+2^k with bit k of a clear, door to triple one-for-one, window ablation, one-bit null at seed 20261018 and at the evolve seed 658750, the decoder battery, the weight comparison, MHD f). Then it (5) writes `results.json`, (6) exits 1 if any step fails or any figure's label differs from the baseline's label, and (7) runs `grimm_scratch/append_dirs.py` plus `lib/append_pipeline.py` (the same chained-manifest code, pointed at this folder, because `append_dirs.py` does not walk `/workspace/pipeline`).

- Expected values are in `expected.json`, each with its source document. They are used only for comparison. No result is hardcoded.
- Labels: **exact** (equal, or equal at the printed decimals), **close** (within the item's stated tolerance), **wrong** (measured otherwise), **not checkable** (no expected value, or no code or data to measure). V3's own claims are kept as `v3claim.*` items whose baseline label is wrong or close, so a change in either direction counts as drift.
- Every figure in `results.json` carries `measured_source`, `expected_source` and `as_of`, or `unknown`.
- `--no-manifest` skips step 7 (for dry runs).
- Baseline files are read and imported, never edited. Runtime is about 90 s on 8 cores (the pytest suite takes most of it).

```

```
This prints, for each claim, HELD or BROKE (or UNVERIFIED/PENDING, which exit 1) with the measured value, the expected value and the counterexample. Other commands: `python3 -m hive list`, `python3 -m hive verify-ledger`, `python3 -m hive run --claims doors,codec --rounds 8`, and `--claims-file examples/claims_from_drive.json`. Tests: `python3 -m pytest -q`.

HIVE generalises `runs/swarm_async/live2.py`. It runs N async bots in five roles over a process pool (one worker per core, capped by available RAM at about 300 MB per worker; on this box that is 8 workers, 4 attackers, 8 measurers and 4 verifiers). A **CAS epoch registry** links a commit only if the epoch it read is still current, and a **P5 recheck** runs inside the lock just before the link. Losers re-sync and retry. A commit is **fail-closed**: it needs an independent peer re-measure (a different seat and a different code path) that reproduces the value exactly. Otherwise a REFUSAL line is written and nothing is linked. Every commit goes into the hash-chained `ledger.jsonl` as an ACTION line plus an OBLIGATION line. A `ledger.jsonl.head` anchor catches truncation, which a chain alone cannot detect.

## baseline_v5/ (new versions; the baseline files are not edited)
- `breaker_v5.py`: the verdict text is computed (λ2 attribution, "repaired uniquely", the /96 and /4512 denominators). The unverifiable "64/170,360" label is removed. Mutants flip the verdicts.

- `ecc_decode_v2.c`: an int64 range guard (|amplitude| ≤ 2^32, weights ≤ 2^20, r ≤ 11). The 2^61 door-lift that baseline C repairs is now REFUSED. Weights are a parameter, with triangular as the default.

--## INSTANCE 1: Fix B — Strictly Convex Confirmation Weights
### 1.1 Setup
The code has N = 48 data positions, j = 0..47. Column j is the 7-bit binary
vector of
c_j = 2j+3 (odd integers 3, 5, …, 97). Every column has bit 0 set.
Define p_j = (c_j − 1)/2 = j+1, ranging over 1..48. This is the upper-bit index.
The confirmation symbol is u = Σ_j w_j · v_j where w_j = f(p_j) for a weight
function f.
Two weight functions are considered:
- Triangular: f(p) = p(p+1)/2
- Squared: f(p) = p²
Both are strictly convex on the integers (Definition: f(tx + (1−t)y) < t·f(x) +
(1−t)·f(y)
for all x ≠ y and t ∈ (0,1); on integers, strict convexity is equivalent to
strictly
increasing forward differences).
The decoder (Section 5 of the spec): repairs position j only when (a) the
syndrome support
equals the support of column j, (b) all nonzero syndrome rows share one value e
(uniform
syndrome), and (c) the confirmation residual q = Σ_j w_j·v_j − u equals e·w_j. A
single-row
syndrome is accepted as a parity edit only when q = 0. Every other syndrome is
refused.
### 1.2 Lemma 1 (Strict Convexity) — PROVED
**Statement.** Let f be strictly convex on the integers. Let a + b = c + d with
{a,b} ≠ {c,d} (as multisets). Then the pair with the larger |x − y| has the
strictly
larger value of f(x) + f(y). In particular, f(a) + f(b) ≠ f(c) + f(d).
**Proof.** Write s = a + b = c + d. Each pair can be written as (s/2 − δ, s/2 +
δ)
with δ ≥ 0, where δ = |x − y|/2. Define g(δ) = f(s/2 − δ) + f(s/2 + δ).
Let 0 ≤ δ₁ < δ₂. The points s/2 ± δ₁ lie strictly inside the closed interval
[s/2 − δ₂, s/2 + δ₂]. Write s/2 + δ₁ = t·(s/2 + δ₂) + (1−t)·(s/2 − δ₂) for
t = (δ₁ + δ₂)/(2δ₂) ∈ (1/2, 1). By strict convexity:
f(s/2 + δ₁) < t·f(s/2 + δ₂) + (1−t)·f(s/2 − δ₂)

 Similarly s/2 − δ₁ = (1−t)·(s/2 + δ₂) + t·(s/2 − δ₂), so:
f(s/2 − δ₁) < (1−t)·f(s/2 + δ₂) + t·f(s/2 − δ₂)
Adding: g(δ₁) < f(s/2 + δ₂) + f(s/2 − δ₂) = g(δ₂). Therefore g is strictly
increasing in δ.
Since {a,b} ≠ {c,d} but a+b = c+d, the two pairs have different δ values
(if δ were equal, the pairs would be identical as multisets). The pair with
larger δ (larger |x−y|, more spread) has strictly larger f-sum. In particular
the f-sums are unequal. ∎
**Computational check.** Verified for all 16,744 quadruples (a,b,c,d) in 1..48
with
a+b = c+d and {a,b} ≠ {c,d}: triangular f-sums never equal, squared f-sums never
equal. (Run 2026-10-19.)
### 1.3 Lemma 2 (Single-Row Relation) — PROVED
**Statement.** For triangular weights, f(a) + f(b) − f(a+b) = −ab. For squared
weights, f(a) + f(b) − f(a+b) = −2ab. In both cases the value is nonzero for a,b
≥ 1.
**Proof.** Triangular: expand directly.
f(a) + f(b) = [a(a+1) + b(b+1)]/2 = [a² + a + b² + b]/2
f(a+b) = (a+b)(a+b+1)/2 = [a² + 2ab + b² + a + b]/2
Subtracting: [a² + a + b² + b − a² − 2ab − b² − a − b]/2 = −2ab/2 = −ab.
Squared: a² + b² − (a+b)² = a² + b² − a² − 2ab − b² = −2ab.
For a, b ≥ 1: −ab ≤ −1 < 0 and −2ab ≤ −2 < 0. Both nonzero. ∎
**Computational check.** Verified for all a,b ∈ 1..48: identity holds exactly,
never zero. (Run 2026-10-19.)
### 1.4 Theorem (Door Family Closed) — PROVED
**Statement.** No ±1 triple of the door family can be accepted by the decoder.
(That is: if +a +b −c reproduces column d via a door, requiring p_a + p_b = p_c
+ p_d,
then the confirmation check fails.)
**Proof.** A door triple +a +b −c reproducing column d means the integer
syndrome
equals ±column d, so the decoder reaches the column-match step. For the decoder
to
accept a wrong repair at d, two conditions must hold: the syndrome must be
uniform
(granted, since it equals ±column d) and the confirmation residual must balance:
f(p_a) + f(p_b) = f(p_c) + f(p_d)
But p_a + p_b = p_c + p_d (door condition on upper-bit indices), and
{p_a, p_b} ≠ {p_c, p_d} (a door redistributes bits between distinct columns;
if the pairs were equal as multisets, the "triple" would not be a triple).
By Lemma 1, f(p_a) + f(p_b) ≠ f(p_c) + f(p_d). The confirmation check fails.
The decoder outputs REFUSED. ∎
**Note.** This proof covers the ±1 door-triple family that the decoder can
mistake.
It does not cover triples with |amplitude| ≠ 1 (those are measured, not proved).

 ### 1.5 Theorem (Single-Row Family Closed) — PROVED
**Statement.** No ±1 triple of the single-row family can be accepted as a tail
edit.
(That is: if +a +b −c leaves only row 0 nonzero, requiring p_c = p_a + p_b, then
the confirmation check q = 0 fails.)
**Proof.** The triple +a +b −c with p_c = p_a + p_b produces an integer syndrome
with only row 0 nonzero (the upper bits cancel: column c = column a + column b
as integer vectors above bit 0, which is exactly p_c = p_a + p_b). The decoder
reaches the single-row step. Acceptance as TAIL_EDIT requires q = 0, i.e.:
f(p_a) + f(p_b) − f(p_c) = 0
But p_c = p_a + p_b, so by Lemma 2 this equals −p_a·p_b (triangular) or
−2·p_a·p_b (squared). Since p_a, p_b ≥ 1, this is nonzero. The confirmation
check fails. The decoder outputs REFUSED. ∎
### 1.6 Theorem (Pair Faults Refused) — PROVED
**Statement.** Every pair fault (+1 on a, −1 on b, a ≠ b) is refused, for any
weight function with pairwise-distinct weights.
**Proof.** The integer syndrome of +a −b is bits(a) − bits(b). For the decoder
to
reach column-match, this must equal e·column(j) for some j and uniform e. The
confirmation residual is w_a − w_b. Acceptance requires w_a − w_b = e·w_j. But
|w_a − w_b| < max(w_a, w_b) ≤ max(w_j) over all j (weights positive and distinct
implies |w_a − w_b| cannot equal e·w_j for integer e ≠ 0 unless {a,b} relates to
j
in a way that the syndrome shape already forbids). More directly: the 124
Hamming-distance-1 pairs produce single-row syndromes, reaching the single-row
step, where acceptance requires q = w_a − w_b = 0, i.e. w_a = w_b, contradicting
distinctness. All other pairs produce multi-row syndromes matching no column

Proof. Row 0 of the syndrome is 1 + 1 − 1 = 1, so e = 1 and col(a) + col(b) − col(c) = col(d) as integer vectors. Reading the columns as integers c_j = 2p_j + 1 gives p_a + p_b = p_c + p_d. Since c ∉ {a, b} and p is injective, p_c ∉ {p_a, p_b}, so {p_a, p_b} ≠ {p_c, p_d} as multisets. [P4] Acceptance needs q = f(p_a) + f(p_b) − f(p_c) = e·w_d = f(p_d), i.e. f(p_a) + f(p_b) = f(p_c) + f(p_d), which Lemma 1 forbids. Refused. ∎
(+,+,+) triples have row 0 equal to 3 and would need three identical columns to be uniform; they never reach the confirmation check.
1.5 Theorem (Single-Row Family Closed) — PROVED
No ±1 triple +a +b −c whose syndrome is a single row is accepted. The upper bits cancel exactly when p_c = p_a + p_b; acceptance needs q = f(p_a) + f(p_b) − f(p_c) = 0, which by Lemma 2 equals −p_a·p_b or −2·p_a·p_b ≠ 0. Refused. ∎
1.6 Theorem (Pair Faults Refused) — PROVED [P5]
Every pair fault with nonzero amplitudes α on a and β on b (a ≠ b) is refused, for any pairwise-distinct weights.
Proof. Let I be the rows set in both columns (row 0 ∈ I), A and B the rows set only in a or only in b. The syndrome is α+β on I, α on A, β on B.
If α + β ≠ 0: row 0 is nonzero, so the syndrome can match e·col(j) only if it is uniform on its support. Uniformity with α, β, α+β all nonzero forces A = B = ∅, i.e. col(a) = col(b), excluded. A single-row syndrome would need A = B = ∅ and |I| = 1, also excluded (columns have weight ≥ 2). Refused.
If α + β = 0: row 0 is zero, and every column has row 0 set, so the syndrome is not e·col(j) for any nonzero e. Its support is A ∪ B. If |A ∪ B| ≥ 2 it matches no column and no single row: refused. If |A ∪ B| = 1 (the 124 Hamming-distance-1 pairs) it reaches the single-row step, where acceptance needs q = α(w_a − w_b) = 0, impossible for distinct weights. Refused. ∎
Computational check. The 124 single-row pairs are exactly the distance-1 pairs, 23/23/23/23/16/16 by flipped bit k = 1..6; all 2,256 equal-magnitude signed pairs, and all 4,512 at magnitudes 2 and 3, are refused by the reference confirmed decoder.
1.7 Measured Results — MEASURED
Also measured (verifier): triangular weights, 20,000 random triples with amplitudes in {±1, ±2, ±3} (unequal allowed): 0 accepted. Boundary: unequal-magnitude triples, faults on u, and quadruples+ are not proved.
INSTANCE 2: V4 — Sidon-Structured Matrix
2.1 Setup
F₆₄ = F₂[t]/(t⁶+t+1). S = {(x, x³) : x ∈ F₆₄}, 64 points of 12 bits. H has r = 14 rows, N = 48 columns; rows 0 and 1 are set in every column; rows 2..13 are 48 of the 63 nonzero points of S at pairwise Hamming distance ≥ 2 (greedy over x = 1..63; x in rows 2..7, x³ in rows 8..13). Masks as in the specification. The decoder is the repair-or-refuse decoder without a confirmation symbol, accepting a single-row syndrome as a parity edit. [P6]
2.2 Theorem (Sidon, characteristic 2) — PROVED
As in the source. Corollary (distinct integer-vector pair sums) — PROVED, holds for every subset of S.
2.3 Theorem (Every Pair and Equal-Magnitude Triple Alias Class Dies) — PROVED [P7]
"Match" means the syndrome equals e·col(j) or e·e_k for some nonzero e.
Case 1 (pairs, any nonzero amplitudes α, β). As in 1.6, with I ⊇ {0, 1}. If α+β ≠ 0, rows 0 and 1 are nonzero (not an axis) and uniformity forces col(a) = col(b). In particular col(a) + col(b) = 2·col(j) would need col(a) = col(b) = col(j), and = 2·e_k is impossible because rows 0 and 1 are both 2 (verified: 0 cases of either). [P8]
Case 2. If α+β = 0, rows 0 and 1 are zero, so no e·col(j) with e ≠ 0 matches (bit 0 of e·col(j) is e ≠ 0). [P9]
Case 3. Its support is the symmetric difference A ∪ B, which has ≥ 2 rows because the minimum pairwise distance is 2 (verified). So no axis matches. [P10]
Case 4 (+,+,+). Rows 0 and 1 carry 3; not an axis; uniform only if the three columns are identical. Refused.
Case 5 (+,+,−) → e·column. Row 0 is 1, so e = 1; col(i) + col(j) − col(k) = col(m) means col(i) + col(j) = col(k) + col(m), a repeated integer pair sum (or col(j) = col(k) if m = i), forbidden by the Corollary.
Case 6 (+,+,−) → e_0: row 1 is 1, not 0. Refused.
Case 7 (+,+,−) → e_m, m ≥ 1: row 0 is 1, not 0. Refused.
(+,−,−) and (−,−,−) are negatives of the above. ∎

class GenCodec:
